One student suggested adding five moles of water to one mole of anhydrous sodium thiosulfate
Their teacher said that method would not work and suggested another method using Hess’s law.
You will carry out the teacher’s method to determine the enthalpy change, ΔH , when one mole of
hydrated sodium thiosulfate, Na S O •5H O, is dissolved in water.
Na S O •5H O(s) + water Na S O (aq)
You will do this by adding a known mass of hydrated sodium thiosulfate to a known volume of
water and measuring the temperature change when the solid dissolves.

must be given.

be used.
Rinse and reuse test-tubes and boiling tubes where possible.
